models.oq.about.heading: About oQ Quantization
models.oq.about.subheading: Compare standard oQ with oQe imatrix and how enhanced quantization works.
models.oq.about.title: oQ: oMLX Universal Dynamic Quantization
models.oq.about.quote1: Quantization should not be exclusive to any particular inference server.
models.oq.about.quote2: oQ produces standard mlx-lm models that work everywhere — oMLX, mlx-lm, LM Studio, and any app that supports MLX safetensors format.
models.oq.about.mixed_precision_heading: oQ and oQe: MLX-native mixed precision
models.oq.about.mixed_precision_body: The quantizer streams tensors from safetensors, measures layer sensitivity, and writes a byte-budgeted mixed-precision checkpoint. Standard oQ focuses on layer-level sensitivity and model-aware protection rules. oQe keeps that same oQ plan and adds imatrix-weighted affine quantization.
models.oq.about.layer_sensitivity_body: is measured with calibration prompts by comparing quantized-layer output error against the float baseline.
models.oq.about.mixed_precision_item_bod: allocates higher bits to sensitive layers and protected tensors while keeping the target bits-per-weight budget under a hard cap.
models.oq.about.architecture_rules_body: keep MoE routers in fp16, protect shared experts and output-critical tensors, leave vision/audio encoders unquantized, and preserve SSM state tensors.
models.oq.about.oqe_adds_body: oQe uses the same oQ sensitivity planner, then adds an importance-matrix calibration step. This is explicitly borrowed from the llama.cpp imatrix idea: collect activation energy from representative prompts, then use that information so quantization spends less error on the input channels that matter most.
models.oq.about.table_oq_best_use: Fast, deterministic conversion with strong baseline quality
models.oq.about.table_oqe_best_use: Better low-bit retention, especially for MoE and activation-skewed layers
models.oq.about.step1_body: oQe runs calibration samples through the model and records average input activation squared, E[x^2], for each quantized Linear input channel.
models.oq.about.step2_body: For MoE SwitchLinear layers, oQe records one importance vector per expert using the router-selected expert indices, so inactive or rarely active experts are visible in the coverage report.
models.oq.about.step3_body: Calibration starts from the requested sample count and can continue up to the adaptive maximum when MoE expert coverage is not sufficient.
models.oq.about.step4_body: During affine quantization, oQe chooses scale/bias candidates by minimizing sum(importance * (weight - dequantized_weight)^2), not plain unweighted MSE.
models.oq.about.fallback_note: If a tensor has no matching imatrix entry, the default behavior is to fall back to standard oQ for that tensor. Enable strict coverage to fail instead.
models.oq.combine_assistant: Combine assistant model as MTP head
models.oq.combine_assistant_help: Merge a separate gemma4_assistant checkpoint into the output as a Lightning MTP head. The output name gets a -mtp suffix and the Lightning MTP toggle works on the result.
models.oq.combine_mtp_donor_help: Graft the MTP head from a same-architecture donor checkpoint (e.g. the base model of a fine-tune) into the quantized output. Tokenizer and geometry must match exactly; the output name gets a -mtp suffix.
models.oq.enhanced_help: Use imatrix calibration to weight affine quantization by activation importance.
models.oq.imatrix_reuse_cache_help: Use a compatible cached imatrix when available; otherwise collect a new one.
models.oq.imatrix_strict_help: Fail when a quantized tensor has no matching imatrix entry instead of falling back to standard oQ.

settings.advanced.burst_decode_hint: Process tokens in batches internally for faster generation. Higher levels run faster but stream in larger chunks; lower levels stream more smoothly. Applies instantly, no restart.
settings.advanced.preserve_mid_system_ca: Preserve Prefix Cache for Mid-Conversation System Notes

When a model's chat template cannot render system or developer messages after the first turn, oMLX rewrites safe trailing notes into the nearest user message so long conversation history can remain prefix-cacheable. Tool call and tool result sequences are left unchanged.
settings.advanced.initial_cache_blocks_h: Blocks pre-allocated at startup. Higher values reduce dynamic allocation overhead.
settings.advanced.hot_cache_write_throug: Keep blocks in RAM AND write them to SSD immediately. Old sessions survive restarts and crashes; recent sessions resume at RAM speed.
settings.advanced.ane_compile_cache_hint: Keep the ANE programs macOS compiles for Qwen prefill so later loads reuse them instead of compiling again. Cuts repeat load time; macOS stores the artifacts in its own cache. Takes effect after a restart.
settings.advanced.gdn_cache_policy_hint: Some models use Gated DeltaNet (GDN) recurrent layers whose state cannot be reconstructed from KV cache blocks alone. An extra state snapshot lets oMLX resume cached prompts without recomputing them.
settings.advanced.gdn_snapshot_storage_h: Auto uses separate SSD files when SSD cache is enabled; otherwise it stores snapshots with the KV cache. With KV Cache follows the same RAM or SSD tier as KV blocks. Enable Hot Cache Only to keep it in RAM.
settings.advanced.gdn_pending_write_limi: Maximum RAM used by encoded snapshots waiting to be written to SSD. When the buffer is full, cache writes pause until space is available.
settings.advanced.gdn_sidecar_state_prec: Controls GDN state stored in SSD sidecars only. FP32 is the exact default. Reduced-precision modes use less space but introduce reconstruction error. Restored state always runs in FP32.
Reduced-precision GDN cache storage can change greedy outputs, break bit-level reproducibility, and reduce output quality. Use FP32 unless you explicitly accept this trade-off.
settings.advanced.sse_keepalive_mode_hin: How streaming HTTP connections stay alive during long prefills. 'Chunk' is most compatible (default). Switch to 'Comment' for the legacy ': keep-alive' format, or 'Off' to disable.

Block diffusion speculative decoding with compatible DFlash and DFlash2 checkpoints.

* MLX impl by bstnxbt(GitHub)
modal.model_settings.dflash_draft_model_: DFlash draft checkpoint (e.g. z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16, z-lab/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-DFlash, z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2, poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-DFlash-NVFP4). Note: -DFlash / -DFlash2 suffix; -assistant variants are for MTP.
modal.model_settings.dflash_quant_hint: Enable quantization for the draft model (weight, activation bits & group size).
modal.model_settings.max_context_fallbac: Prompts at or above this token count switch to BatchedEngine. Leave empty for unlimited.
modal.model_settings.draft_window_size_h: Draft model sliding-attention window. Helps stabilise acceptance on long contexts. Leave empty for dflash default (2048).
modal.model_settings.draft_sink_size_hin: Attention-sink tokens always kept regardless of window. Leave empty for dflash default (0).
modal.model_settings.runtime_block_size_: Maximum draft and verify tokens per cycle. Leave empty to use the checkpoint block size.
modal.model_settings.verify_mode_hint: Verifier algorithm. "adaptive" shrinks block size when acceptance drops; "off" disables speculative verify.
modal.model_settings.in_memory_cache_hin: DFlash L1 prefix snapshot cache in RAM. Speeds up multi-turn chats with shared prefixes.
modal.model_settings.in_memory_cache_max: Maximum number of prefix snapshots kept in L1 cache. Each entry stores KV + draft GDN state for one conversation prefix.
modal.model_settings.in_memory_cache_siz: Byte budget for L1 snapshots; LRU evicts when exceeded.
modal.model_settings.ssd_cache_hint_html: L2 spill of evicted L1 entries to disk. Uses the oMLX paged SSD cache directory (dflash_l2/).
modal.model_settings.ssd_cache_unavailab: Enable oMLX paged SSD cache first (--paged-ssd-cache-dir).
modal.model_settings.ssd_cache_requires_: Requires in-memory cache to be enabled.
modal.model_settings.ssd_cache_size_hint: Disk budget for L2 spill; oldest entries are evicted when exceeded.
modal.model_settings.enable_thinking_hin: Enable reasoning/thinking mode for this model.
modal.model_settings.thinking_budget_hin: Limit thinking tokens for reasoning models. Forces end of thinking when exceeded.
modal.model_settings.guided_grammar_hint: Apply an EBNF grammar by default for this model.
modal.model_settings.limit_tool_result_h: Truncate large tool results (e.g. file reads) to a token limit
modal.model_settings.turboquant_kv_hint: Compress KV cache using vector quantization. Lower bits = more compression, higher bits = better quality. Supports 2 to 8 bits.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_hint: Split eligible Qwen 3.5/3.6/3.8 prompt-processing work across both ANEs and the GPU. This uses private Apple runtime interfaces and applies after the model reloads.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_dual_hint: Pin one resident program to each physical ANE instance.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_gdn_hint: Also split eligible GDN input projections across the ANEs and GPU.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_cpu_hint: Requires a separate Qwen q4 checkpoint clone with floating tensors converted to FP16. Retune the MLP ANE share when enabled.
modal.model_settings.qwen_ane_cpu_schedu: Uses Apple's shared-resource scheduler hint and falls back automatically when unsupported. Eight workers is the measured starting point.

bench.heading: Performance Benchmark
bench.description: Measure inference speed for single requests and continuous batching. All other models will be unloaded before benchmarking.
bench.config.context_hint: It only affects results when acceleration features such as MTP or DFlash are enabled.
bench.config.force_lm_engine_hint: Use mlx-lm for this benchmark. VLM MTP drafters are ignored, so results measure the LM-only baseline.
bench.config.external_hint: Benchmark a remote OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint instead of a local model. The endpoint must support streaming usage (stream_options.include_usage).
bench.config.ane_aligned_prompt_hint: Runs PP4097/8193/etc. so prefill contains exact 2,048-token blocks. These diagnostic results stay local.

bench.metrics.ttft.name: TTFT
bench.metrics.test.tooltip: Test case label in the format ppN/tgM. 'pp' = prompt processing (number of input tokens), 'tg' = token generation (number of output tokens). For example, pp1024/tg256 means 1024 input tokens and 256 output tokens.
bench.metrics.ttft.tooltip: Time to First Token — how long the user waits before seeing any output. The model must read and process the entire prompt (prefill phase) before generating the first token. Longer prompts = higher TTFT. Measured in milliseconds. Lower is better.
bench.metrics.tpot.tooltip: Time Per Output Token — average interval between consecutive output tokens during the generation (decode) phase. Directly affects how fast text appears on screen. For example, 20ms/tok means ~50 tokens per second. Lower is better.
bench.metrics.tg_tps.tooltip: Token Generation TPS — number of output tokens produced per second during the decode phase. This is the inverse of TPOT (e.g., TPOT 20ms = 50 tg TPS). The primary measure of how fast the model writes its response. Higher is better.
bench.metrics.pp_tps.tooltip: Prompt Processing TPS — how many input tokens the model processes per second during the prefill phase. Higher values mean the model reads your prompt faster, which directly reduces TTFT. Important for long-context workloads. Higher is better.
bench.metrics.e2e.tooltip: End-to-End Latency — total wall-clock time from sending the request to receiving the complete response. Equals TTFT + (TPOT x number of output tokens). This is the overall time the user waits for a full answer.
bench.metrics.throughput.tooltip: Total Throughput — combined input and output tokens processed per second. Shows overall system utilization including both prefill and generation. Useful for comparing total compute efficiency across different prompt lengths.
bench.metrics.peak_mem.tooltip: Peak GPU Memory — maximum GPU (unified) memory used during inference for this test case. Includes model weights, KV cache, and intermediate activations. Helps estimate how large a model your hardware can handle.
bench.metrics.batch_size.tooltip: Batch Size — number of requests processed simultaneously. Batching lets the GPU handle multiple requests at once, increasing total throughput but adding some latency per individual request. A 2x batch doesn't mean 2x speed due to memory bandwidth limits.
bench.metrics.speedup.tooltip: Speedup — how much faster token generation is compared to a single request (1x baseline). For example, 1.8x means batching produces tokens 1.8 times faster overall. Values above 1x show more efficient GPU utilization through batching.
bench.metrics.pp_tps_req.tooltip: Per-Request Prompt Processing TPS — the pp TPS divided by the batch size. Shows how fast each individual request's prompt is processed when sharing the GPU with other requests. Expect this to be lower than the single-request pp TPS since compute is shared.
bench.metrics.avg_ttft.tooltip: Average Time to First Token across all requests in the batch. Higher than single-request TTFT because the GPU must process multiple prompts. Shows the typical wait time each user experiences under batched workloads.
bench.metrics.ttft.description: Latency until the model starts responding. Measures prompt processing (prefill) speed. Lower is better.
bench.metrics.tpot.name: TPOT
bench.metrics.tpot.description: Average time between each generated token. Measures decode speed. Lower is better.
bench.metrics.tg_tps.name: tg TPS
bench.metrics.tg_tps.description: Output tokens generated per second. Inverse of TPOT. Higher is better.
bench.metrics.pp_tps.name: pp TPS
bench.metrics.pp_tps.description: Input/prompt tokens processed per second during prefill. Higher is better.
bench.metrics.e2e.name: E2E Latency
bench.metrics.e2e.description: Total time from request submission to complete response. Includes prefill + generation.
bench.metrics.throughput.name: Total Throughput
bench.metrics.throughput.description: Overall tokens (input + output) per second. Measures total system utilization.
bench.metrics.batch_size.name: Batch Size
bench.metrics.batch_size.description: Number of concurrent requests processed together. Higher batch sizes improve total throughput but increase per-request latency.
bench.metrics.speedup.name: Speedup
bench.metrics.speedup.description: Token generation throughput multiplier compared to single-request baseline (1x). Higher is better.
bench.metrics.pp_tps_req.name: pp TPS/req
bench.metrics.pp_tps_req.description: Prompt processing throughput divided by batch size. Shows per-request prefill speed under batching load.
ctx_bench.heading: Context Benchmark
ctx_bench.description: Measure the largest context window this machine can actually prefill for a model. The result is written into the model's Context Window setting.
ctx_bench.config.target_hint: The benchmark searches up to this size. Larger targets take longer to verify. Sizes beyond the selected model's native context are hidden.
ctx_bench.config.priority_hint: Mirrors the global Prefill Priority setting and saves immediately — serving uses the same mode, so the measured value stays valid.
ctx_bench.warning.title: Before you start
ctx_bench.warning.long_time: This benchmark can take a long time — the verification prefill runs a real prompt at the measured size, which may take many minutes for large models and targets.
ctx_bench.warning.unload: All loaded models are unloaded when the benchmark starts, interrupting any active requests.
ctx_bench.warning.autoapply: When the benchmark finishes, the measured value is automatically applied to the model's Context Window setting.
ctx_bench.result.applied_note: The value has been applied to this model's Context Window setting.
ctx_bench.result.snapshot_note: The result reflects free memory and the Memory Guard tier at benchmark time; rerun after major changes to either.
acc_bench.heading: Intelligence Benchmark
acc_bench.description: Evaluate model intelligence across knowledge, reasoning, math, and coding benchmarks. All other models will be unloaded before benchmarking.
acc_bench.config.benchmarks_hint: Fixed seed sampling ensures the same questions across different models for fair comparison. Select Full for the complete dataset.
acc_bench.config.livecodebench_warning: LiveCodeBench executes model-generated code on your machine (sandboxed with timeout and memory limits).
acc_bench.config.batch_size_hint: Process multiple questions concurrently. Higher batch size = faster but uses more memory.
acc_bench.config.thinking_hint: Defaults to model's Enable Thinking setting. Auto-detects if the model thinks even when disabled.
acc_bench.config.sampling_hint: Deterministic (greedy) keeps scores reproducible across runs. Enable to use the model's configured sampling (temperature, top-p) for a real-world score.
acc_bench.config.external_hint: Evaluate a remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of a local model. Thinking mode is disabled; requests never send enable_thinking.
acc_bench.config.external_extra_body_hin: Optional provider-specific request parameters. For example, DeepSeek V4 accepts {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}. Leave empty to send none.
acc_bench.config.external_max_tokens_hin: Optional floor for each question's max_tokens; benchmark defaults are never lowered (e.g. LiveCodeBench keeps 16384). Thinking models spend reasoning tokens against this budget — MMLU's default 128 is usually exhausted mid-reasoning, so set e.g. 8192.
acc_bench.results.reliability_warning: This test includes empty responses, truncation, or API errors. Its accuracy may be unreliable and should not be compared directly with local models.
